Subject: Security intake & private deployment next steps — Avanta Health

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we stay aligned: 

Call recap (high level):
- Avanta is evaluating Redwood for document-processing and patient-data summarization workloads.
- Primary requirement: HIPAA-compliant private deployment with strong network isolation (VPC + optional air-gapped path for PHI batch jobs).
- Compliance guardrails: SOC 2 Type II, data residency in us-east-1, and contractual DPA/GDPR clauses for EU data if/when needed.

Action items we committed to:
1) Avanta -> share SOC 2 report and current vendor questionnaire answers (security@avantahealth).
2) Redwood -> provide a concise private-deploy checklist and a short (1–2 page) network-boundary diagram showing options: managed VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or on-prem air-gapped ingestion path.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) to walk topology and firewall requirements.

Immediate asks for you:
- Please attach the most recent SOC 2 Type II (redacted as needed).
- Fill out the attached vendor_questionnaire.docx where you can; leave any legal/contract items blank and we’ll loop in Legal.
- Confirm whether you prefer: \"VPC peering\" or \"on-prem air-gapped batch\" as the primary path so we prioritize the diagram.

Internal notes: Sean/Marissa/Ben — I flagged this as high priority; Avanta is aiming for a decision window by end of month.

Attachments: vendor_questionnaire.docx (please start with section A: infrastructure & encryption)

Thanks — Sofia

Answers to your immediate questions:
- Preference: we want VPC peering first (lower ops overhead), with an air-gap option for scheduled PHI exports as a backup.
- Data residency: production in us-east-1 only for now.
- Timeline: procurement needs an architecture diagram and a short list of required controls before the legal review; roughly a 10–14 day window to get internal approvals.

Next call: can we do a technical deep-dive on Monday 10/19 at 10 am PT? Marissa joining would be great.

I’ve attached the SOC 2 PDF and a scanned note from security (comments will come in the questionnaire docx).

Subject: Re: Security intake & private deployment next steps — diagram & notes

Tom / Sofia — attaching a first-pass network diagram and a short notes sheet (network_diagram_v1.png referenced; link to full doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_diagram). Highlights: 

Option A — VPC peering (recommended first step):
- Peered VPC in Avanta account with cross-account role for instance provisioning.
- Egress locked behind a NAT + strict outbound ACLs; PrivateLink used for metadata/service endpoints.
- KV cache stored in customer KMS; we recommend envelope encryption and no external egress logging to the public internet.

Option B — On-prem air-gapped path (batch PHI exports):
- SFTP staging inside an air-gapped subnet; automated import window using signed USB transfer or isolated transfer node in a hardened DMZ.
- This option requires scheduled maintenance windows and an additional Ops playbook for emergency access.

Next items from our side:
- I’ll refine the diagram for Monday's call and annotate ports (SSH, TLS endpoints, ephemeral ports for data sync).
- Sean/Ben — please confirm the checklist items I should include for firewall and KMS oversight.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- For VPC peering, do you support route-table-based restrictions per-subnet (we need microsegmentation)?
- For the air-gapped flow: what tooling do you recommend for tamper-evident batch transfers?

If you can add those two call bullets to the agenda, that would help us triage. I’ll send the draft questionnaire by Friday.

Thanks — Tom
